editorial:
Imagine being so handsome that you can practically print money just by smiling at wealthy women. That is exactly how the main character, nicknamed Angel's Face, spends his days. He lives a life of luxury and easy money until he meets Loina, a fancy decorator who is just as greedy and driven as he is. They make a perfect match because they both love the finer things in life and aren't afraid to play the game to get them. The vibe is very classic and dramatic, showing you a world of high fashion and low morals where beauty is a tool for survival.

You will really enjoy how the chemistry between the two leads pulls you in, even if they aren't exactly good people. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow by today's standards. The best part is watching the emotional shift when money stops being the only thing that matters. If you enjoy old-school dramas, you should definitely try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a quiet weekend night when you want something stylish and thoughtful.
endingExplained: After Loina hits rock bottom and leaves, Angel's Face almost rushes to save her. However, a loyal friend talks him out of it, reminding him that their relationship was built on greed. This wake-up call hits him hard. He stops chasing wealthy women and luxury. The movie ends with him looking inward and deciding to change his ways, finally choosing to settle down and live an honest, quiet life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic French cinema and stories about redemption.
